newsitem.title: UK: British war crimes hearing adjourned for two weeks.
newsitem.headline: British war crimes hearing adjourned for two weeks.

text.p: A hearing preparing for Britain's first war crimes trial was adjourned for two weeks on Wednesday to allow the prosecution time to gather more evidence.
Szymon Serafinowicz, an 85-year-old refugee from the former Soviet Union, is facing three charges of murdering Jews in Byelorussia (now Belarus) during World War Two.
Prosecutor John Nutting requested the adjournment "to make further inquiries" but gave no details about what evidence he was seeking.
The hearing, expected to last about three days, will now begin on November 6. The full trial is due to start on January 6, 1997.
Serafinowicz, a tiny, white-haired man who appears very frail, was in court for the hearing which lasted only about five minutes. He nodded and muttered inaudibly when asked to confirm his identity.
His trial will be the first under Britain's controversial War Crimes Act, which the government had to invoke special powers to force through parliament in 1991.
Serafinowicz has denied the charges although he has not yet made a plea in court.
